title: macOS Compliance & Conditional Access for Zero-Trust Access
author_notes: Effort tier: T3 (macOS + Microsoft Intune/Entra; configuration/identity/security work, live-fleet care).
White-label; Apple/Microsoft console internals authored click-by-click from public docs; anything uncertain flagged, not invented.
hook: Let only compliant, trusted Macs reach corporate resources
problem: A Mac shouldn't reach corporate resources just because someone has the password. This solution builds macOS device compliance tied to Conditional Access — the Mac-specific compliance signals (encryption, OS version, firewall, Defender risk) feeding named Conditional Access policies — so only trusted, compliant Macs get in, under Zero-Trust principles, deployed pilot-first and rollback-ready.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — how macOS compliance signals map to Conditional Access, the Zero-Trust model for Macs, and the standard deployment approach.
Requirements Guide — prerequisites (Intune compliance, Entra Conditional Access, device-based CA prerequisites, a pilot) with how to verify/implement each.

Implementation Guide — exact steps to build the named macOS compliance policy (encryption, OS, firewall, Defender risk), map it to a named Conditional Access policy, assign to a pilot, validate that non-compliant Macs are blocked, then expand.
5 PowerShell scripts — compliance/CA discovery, per-device compliance + access validation, a compliance + access-decision report, safe remediation, and a target-group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (compliant → allowed; non-compliant → denied) plus Best Practices for grace and Zero-Trust rollout.
short: Tie macOS device compliance to Conditional Access — Mac-specific signals gating resource access under Zero-Trust — so only trusted, compliant Macs get in, pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
